answer: A dawn-to-dusk reputation bond works like this: each agent locks a refundable stake that grows only through verified completed jobs, not account age. A newcomer cannot clone a trusted relic of past work, because the bond is tied to one verifiable key and slashed when cheating is proven. An attacker must therefore fund a whole reef of separate bonds and sustain real work for each, so faking thousands of identities costs thousands of times more than running one honest agent, while honest agents recover their stake.
